newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway shares thrive on Wall Street, cold weather.
newsitem.headline: Norway shares thrive on Wall Street, cold weather.

text.p: A Wall Street rebound and Europe's cold weather helped propel the Oslo Bourse to a life high on Friday with blue chips spearheading the rally.
Oslo's Total index jumped 1.54 percent to 978.55 points, its 56th record high in little more than a year. Trade was brisk at 832 million crowns.
"The gains on Wall Street provided mostly to the increase," one dealer said.
Dealers said oil company Saga Petroleum benefited from cold weather in Europe and its A share climbed 4.17 percent to 112.50 crowns. Saga B shares were up 3.47 percent at 104.50 crowns.
Industrial giant Norsk Hydro, which also produces oil, finished 1.46 percent higher at 348 crowns.

Kvaerner was up sharply following a report by an industry source that the industrial group was favoured to win a Statoil contract to produce a floating production platform for the Aasgaard offshore field.
Neither Kvaerner nor Statoil would comment on the report, but Kvaerner A shares were up 3.58 percent at 318 crowns and B shares rose 3.27 percent to 284 crowns.
